"""Semantic version parsing, comparison, and range matching.

Versions follow Semantic Versioning 2.0.0: ``MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH``, then an
optional pre-release (``-`` followed by dot-separated identifiers) and an
optional build (``+`` followed by dot-separated identifiers). Identifiers
are non-empty and made of ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens. Numeric parts
(MAJOR, MINOR, PATCH, and all-digit pre-release identifiers) must not have
leading zeros. Anything else is invalid and raises ``ValueError``.

Precedence (``compare``) follows the SemVer 2.0.0 rules: compare MAJOR,
MINOR, and PATCH numerically; a version with a pre-release is lower than
the same version without one; pre-release identifiers are compared left to
right, all-digit ones numerically and the rest in ASCII order, with
all-digit identifiers lower than the rest, and a shorter list lower when
all its identifiers equal the start of a longer one. Build metadata is
ignored.

Ranges (``satisfies``) are one or more comparator sets joined by ``||``; a
version satisfies the range if it satisfies any set. A set is one or more
comparators separated by whitespace, all of which must hold. A comparator
is a full version optionally prefixed by an operator:

- ``=`` (or no operator), ``>``, ``>=``, ``<``, ``<=``: by precedence.
- ``^X.Y.Z``: at least ``X.Y.Z`` and below the next version that changes
  the leftmost non-zero part, i.e. ``^1.2.3`` is ``>=1.2.3 <2.0.0``,
  ``^0.2.3`` is ``>=0.2.3 <0.3.0``, and ``^0.0.3`` is ``>=0.0.3 <0.0.4``.
- ``~X.Y.Z``: at least ``X.Y.Z`` and below ``X.(Y+1).0``.

A version with a pre-release satisfies a set only if some comparator in
that set has a pre-release on the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (so
``1.2.3-beta.2`` satisfies ``>=1.2.3-beta.1`` but not ``>=1.0.0``).
Invalid ranges raise ``ValueError``.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass

    minor: int
    patch: int
    prerelease: tuple[str, ...] = ()

    raise NotImplementedError

"""Semantic version parsing, comparison, and range matching.

Versions follow Semantic Versioning 2.0.0: ``MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH``, then an
optional pre-release (``-`` followed by dot-separated identifiers) and an
optional build (``+`` followed by dot-separated identifiers). Identifiers
are non-empty and made of ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens. Numeric parts
(MAJOR, MINOR, PATCH, and all-digit pre-release identifiers) must not have
leading zeros. Anything else is invalid and raises ``ValueError``.

Precedence (``compare``) follows the SemVer 2.0.0 rules: compare MAJOR,
MINOR, and PATCH numerically; a version with a pre-release is lower than
the same version without one; pre-release identifiers are compared left to
right, all-digit ones numerically and the rest in ASCII order, with
all-digit identifiers lower than the rest, and a shorter list lower when
all its identifiers equal the start of a longer one. Build metadata is
ignored.

Ranges (``satisfies``) are one or more comparator sets joined by ``||``; a
version satisfies the range if it satisfies any set. A set is one or more
comparators separated by whitespace, all of which must hold. A comparator
is a full version optionally prefixed by an operator:

- ``=`` (or no operator), ``>``, ``>=``, ``<``, ``<=``: by precedence.
- ``^X.Y.Z``: at least ``X.Y.Z`` and below the next version that changes
  the leftmost non-zero part, i.e. ``^1.2.3`` is ``>=1.2.3 <2.0.0``,
  ``^0.2.3`` is ``>=0.2.3 <0.3.0``, and ``^0.0.3`` is ``>=0.0.3 <0.0.4``.
- ``~X.Y.Z``: at least ``X.Y.Z`` and below ``X.(Y+1).0``.

A version with a pre-release satisfies a set only if some comparator in
that set has a pre-release on the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (so
``1.2.3-beta.2`` satisfies ``>=1.2.3-beta.1`` but not ``>=1.0.0``).
Invalid ranges raise ``ValueError``.
"""

All five modules in `devkit/` are implemented as their docstrings describe. They use only the standard library and work on Python 3.9.

I tested them with a throwaway script of about 150 checks: the examples from each docstring, the error cases, and edge cases. All pass. What each module does:

- **`semver`**: parsing follows the SemVer 2.0.0 rules, including rejecting leading zeros and invalid identifiers, and comparison follows the standard precedence rules. `^` and `~` are turned into a lower and upper bound, and the pre-release rule only lets a pre-release version match a set that names a pre-release of the same `X.Y.Z`. An invalid range raises `ValueError` even if an earlier `||` set already matched.
- **`cron`**: names (`MON-FRI`, `feb`) and steps like `5/20` work, 7 counts as Sunday, and `*/1` counts as restricted for the day-of-month/day-of-week "either" rule. It checks day by day, so a schedule that never fires (like `* * 31 2 *`) fails within about 1 ms.
- **`duration`**: whole seconds parse as `int` and fractional ones as `float`. Formatting never uses scientific notation, so 1e-7 seconds is written `PT0.0000001S`.
- **`table`**: rows survive a write-then-read round trip, including cells containing `|` or a trailing backslash.
- **`ini`**: values are cached as they're filled in, and `$$` becomes a literal `$` that isn't filled in again.

Decisions the docstrings didn't cover:

- **Whitespace in ranges and versions:** `> 1.0.0` (with a space) is rejected, because the docstring says the operator is a prefix. Versions with surrounding whitespace or a leading `v` are also invalid.
- **Time zones in `duration.add`:** with a time-zone-aware datetime, the week/day/time parts are added through UTC. This makes "exact elapsed time" correct across daylight-saving changes; plain Python arithmetic would add wall-clock time instead. Naive datetimes behave as you'd expect.
- **`cron` near year 9999:** times past `datetime.max` raise `ValueError`, not `OverflowError`.
- **`ini` references:** `${section:key}` splits at the last colon, because keys can't contain `:` but section names can. An unclosed `${` is left as literal text.
- **`parse_table`:** blank lines before and after the table are ignored.
